chunk-001:d73-c001-02.proposition: Libertarian freedom fits the experienced structure of deliberation as serious consideration of genuine options followed by the agent's selection and action.

chunk-001:d73-c001-04.proposition: Popular scientific presentations overstate the case against free will because unresolved philosophical questions about causation and time prevent treating the issue as empirically settled.

chunk-001:d73-c001-05.proposition: Practical deliberation is a directed process integrating imagined options, rational and emotional evaluation, and valitional control rather than a passive succession of appearing thoughts.

chunk-001:d73-c001-10.proposition: Indeterminism need not be randomness, since probabilistic variation within constraints can leave genuine options open without making a choice chaotic or reasonless.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-04.proposition: Agent causation and criterial neural causation each provide a coherent model in which the person originates action without a prior sufficient physical cause.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-06.proposition: Despite inherited biological and social limits, agents contribute to self-realization through repeated choices that reshape their dispositions, abilities, and future possibilities.

chunk-002:chunk002-candidate-10.proposition: Undetermined neural firing supplies openness while system-level criterial causation supplies top-down personal control, avoiding both prior sufficient determination and mere event-level randomness.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Moral responsibility can rest on a person's accumulated contribution to character through many earlier decisions, alongside libertarian alternative possibilities and sourcehood.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Because evolved deliberation and inquiry are practically effective and inherently consider possibilities, a pragmatist should treat their embedded conception of agency and alternatives as true.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Ordinary interpretation distinguishes intentional agency from compelled conduct caused by shoving or pathology, so source-like agency cannot consistently be confined to one's own first-person standpoint.
